41: Correlated predictors can destabilize linear-model coefficients; PCA creates orthogonal components in a reduced feature space.

42: A prior distribution must match the variable's support and the assumptions about the process generating it.
Poisson models nonnegative event counts with unbounded support. Calling elapsed waiting minutes discrete does not establish a Poisson process.
Uniform waiting on a regular 10-minute interval would require uniformly timed arrivals and would have mean 5, conflicting with the stated mean 3.
An ordinary normal distribution allows negative and arbitrarily large waits and does not match a bounded discrete waiting variable without modifications.
A binomial distribution requires a fixed number of Bernoulli trials and a success probability. Those assumptions are absent, so no unique prior is determined.

Multiple imputation uses the other informative columns to estimate missing entries, preserving relationships more effectively than a single constant fill.
A single mean ignores relationships with other columns and artificially reduces variation in the imputed feature.
